content.text:
`slugify(text)` is now implemented in `src/strings.js`, and `npm test` passes all 13 tests (the 2 existing `capitalize` tests plus 11 new ones).

It follows your rules in this order:
- Converts `đ`/`Đ` to `d`.
- Strips diacritics.
- Lowercases.
- Turns each run of non-`a-z0-9` characters into one hyphen.
- Trims the leading hyphen.
- Cuts to 50 characters.
- Trims any trailing hyphen left by the cut.

Non-string input is converted with `String(text)`, so `null` becomes `'null'` rather than throwing.

I added the new tests to `test/strings.test.js`. They cover:
- Basic hyphenation, collapsing runs of symbols, and trimming.
- Vietnamese text, `đ`/`Đ`, and other Latin accents.
- Digits.
- Empty and symbol-only input.
- The 50-character cut, including a cut that would otherwise end in a hyphen, and a slug of exactly 50 characters.
